speaker: narrator_main
text: Eight billion people.

speaker: narrator_main
text: Today, our species floods every continent with electric light, yet a single volcanic trap almost erased our bloodline.

speaker: narrator_main
text: Yet seventy-four thousand years ago, every living ancestor of modern humanity could have sheltered inside one narrow valley.

speaker: char_sena_74000bce
text: The sun is vanishing, Kael.

speaker: char_sena_74000bce
text: Feel this dust, Kael. Warm ash falls like snow, yet it cuts the skin.

speaker: narrator_main
text: What settled onto her palm in northwestern Ethiopia was not woodsmoke, nor desert sand, but razor-sharp shards of volcanic glass.

speaker: char_kael_74000bce
text: The eastern mountains are quiet. Nothing burns there.

speaker: narrator_main
text: Kael was right about the local peaks, because the killer lay four thousand miles away.

speaker: narrator_main
text: Across the Indian Ocean, an island had just ruptured with a violence Earth had not seen in two million years.

speaker: narrator_main
text: Beneath northern Sumatra, five colossal chambers of silica-rich rhyolite magma had been pressurizing for centuries like a planetary landmine.

speaker: narrator_main
text: Then the roof failed.

speaker: narrator_main
text: When Mount Toba detonated seventy-four thousand years ago, it registered Category Eight on the Volcanic Explosivity Index, shattering the ceiling of geological history.

speaker: narrator_main
text: Compare it to Mount Saint Helens in nineteen eighty: Toba was ten thousand times larger.

speaker: narrator_main
text: Every ten minutes, the vent hurled a full cubic kilometer of pulverized rock into the sky, sustaining that fury for two weeks.

speaker: narrator_main
text: Nothing within hundreds of miles survived.

speaker: narrator_main
text: In total, two thousand eight hundred cubic kilometers of dense magma tore out of the earth, leaving a hundred-kilometer crater behind.

speaker: narrator_main
text: Superheated co-ignimbrite columns punched thirty-two kilometers upward, piercing straight through the tropopause into the dry stratosphere.

speaker: narrator_main
text: Yet lava was not the weapon.

speaker: narrator_main
text: Had Toba erupted in winter, winds would have dumped its ash harmlessly into the southern ocean—but Toba erupted in summer.

speaker: narrator_main
text: Caught by the northern summer monsoon, the stratospheric plume locked onto a collision course with the heart of the ancient world.

speaker: narrator_main
text: And inside that cloud rode a chemical payload capable of switching off the sun across the entire planet.

speaker: narrator_main
text: Within hours, noon across the Indian subcontinent darkened into a suffocating, pitch-black midnight laced with volcanic lightning.

speaker: narrator_main
text: Fifteen centimeters of abrasive tephra blanketed the entire peninsula, while river valleys choked under ash drifts six meters deep.

speaker: narrator_main
text: Water turned to toxic sludge.

speaker: narrator_main
text: Fluorine and sulfuric acid leached into streams, stripping leaves from trees and blinding grazing herds before they could flee the valleys.
